title: Tailwatch: microservice latency & cost diary (synthetic workloads)
content:
Purpose
This is a working diary of a small synthetic benchmark sweep aimed at surfacing tail-behavior interactions between microservice-style frontends and the inference runtime under multi-tenant vs dedicated modes. The goal: capture compact, shareable artifacts (ASCII charts + annotated notes) that product and runtime teams can act on quickly.

Scope and motivation
- Focus: 1) 95th/99th/99.9th latency slices for short session requests (prompt length 16–64 tokens), 2) cost delta per 1k requests across config shapes (dedicated GPU vCPU-backed proxying), 3) how brief cold spikes/bursts shift percentiles.
- Workloads are synthetic but mirror mobile chat behavior: 40% single-turn (16 tokens), 40% short session (32 tokens), 20% long/chain (64 tokens). Interarrival modeled as Poisson with mean RPS = 60 for baseline, scaled to 180 for spike scenarios.

Environment and configs tested
- Runtime A: dedicated inference pool (rwinf-dedicated-gpu-v2), 80GB LLM runtime, KV cache enabled, quantized int8.
- Runtime B: shared multi-tenant GPU pool (rwinf-shared-gpu), opportunistic slot preemption enabled.
- Proxy: gRPC frontend microservice in front of runtime, two replicas (proxy-small), placed in same AZ.
- Instrumentation: tracing via console-agent, percentiles computed from request latency at proxy exit (end-to-end).
- Cost model: amortized token GPU time + proxy CPU cost. For simplicity use internal cost factors: GPU-minute = $0.85, vCPU-minute = $0.02, token-compute normalized to 0.00012 GPU-min/token.

Key experimental knobs recorded
- KV cache hit rate: synthetic: low(12%), med(46%), high(78%).
- Warm pool size (dedicated only): 0 (cold), 2 (warm), 6 (prewarm).
- Batch window (ms): 0, 6, 12.
- Preemption aggressiveness (shared pool): low | medium | high.

High-level findings (short summary)
1) Median latency between dedicated and shared comparable at baseline RPS=60; divergence appears at 95th+ under bursts.
2) 99.9th latency is dominated by opportunistic preempts & proxy queueing; dedicated prewarm eliminates ~60–75% of 99.9th tail in our runs.
3) Cost per 1k requests: dedicated with high prewarm is ~1.3x higher than shared at base load, but during frequent spikes (sustained 3x RPS) shared cost rises 2.2x due to repeated cold starts and longer GPU occupancy.
4) KV cache gives strong amortized win for conversational flows; even a modest 45% cache hit shifts 95th by ~12–18% and reduces token GPU-min by ~24%.

Annotated ASCII charts and tables
1) Percentile latency snapshot (RPS=60, medium cache, batch window 6ms) - latencies in ms.

Service | p50 | p95 | p99 | p99.9 | notes
------- | ---- | ---- | ---- | ------ | -----
dedicated | 48 | 92 | 160 | 430 | prewarm=2
shared    | 51 | 112 | 260 | 960 | preempt=medium

Interpretation: median similar, but tail explodes on shared. 99.9th x2.2–2.5 higher.

2) Tail behavior under spike (3x for 60s) - combined timeline summary (ASCII sparkline-like):
- Dedicated prewarm=6:  p99.9 trend: 420 430 445 430 415 420 430
- Dedicated prewarm=0:  p99.9 trend: 900 1200 1500 1300 1000 950 980
- Shared preempt=high:  p99.9 trend: 1800 2100 2700 3500 3000 2200 2000

Quick note: lines above are representative per-10s checkpoints across the 60s burst. Dedicated with prewarm tightens the series and avoids huge outliers.

3) Cost per 1k requests (approx), baseline RPS=60, 24-hour equivalent amortization
Configuration | GPU-min per 1k req | vCPU-min per 1k req | cost ($/1k)
------------- | ------------------ | ------------------- | ----------
dedicated prewarm=6 | 2.6 | 4.8 | 3.2
dedicated prewarm=0 | 3.1 | 4.6 | 3.6
shared preempt=medium | 1.9 | 5.2 | 2.7
shared preempt=high (bursting) | 4.6 | 6.4 | 5.6

Note: shared at base appears cheaper; during bursting it becomes expensive because cold starts cause longer GPU minutes per request and proxy CPU overhead due to retries/backpressure.

4) KV cache sensitivity (95th latency, dedicated prewarm=2, batch window=6ms):
KV hit | p95 (ms) | % improvement vs no-cache
------ | ------- | ---------------------------
12% | 108 | -0% (baseline)
46% | 95  | 12%
78% | 81  | 25%

Actionable: investing in higher cache hit (prefetch or affinity) buys tail reduction and cost efficiency.

Open questions and TODOs
- Need to instrument per-request GPU-occupancy to confirm whether longer occupancy on shared is due to kernel fusion differences or repeated reinitialization. (Linked: GH bench PR#78)
- Run the same sweep with 128-token tails and a different model to test memory pressure interactions (we only tested up to 64 tokens).
- Explore proxy backpressure tuning: should the frontend shed load earlier or queue longer? Add test where proxy soft-shed at queue depth 200.
- Repeat with v2 batch scheduler (alpha) to see if batching reduces shared burst penalty.

Design notes for product/console collateral (how this could be shown)
- A small explainer widget: "tail delta" card that shows p99.9 cost-adjusted impact for a route (dedicated vs shared). Use a 7-point sparkline + single-number unit-econ multiplier (e.g., x1.4 cost at 99.9 tail).
- Add a KV-hit slider in the console scenario planner to let users simulate how affinity/prewarm affects tail & cost (sensitivity table like above).
- Provide exported text tables (CSV) for quick copy-paste into PRs; keep the ASCII representation as a human-readable preview in the console.

Experiment log (short timestamped notes)
2026-08-03 09:12 - baseline runs kick off (RPS=60), dedicated prewarm=2, shared preempt=medium.
2026-08-03 09:34 - observed first p99.9 spike on shared up to 2.1s, traced to proxy retry loop (ticket TAL-421).
2026-08-03 10:05 - enabled prewarm=6 on dedicated; p99.9 drops ~62% in next run.
2026-08-03 10:42 - simulated 60s 3x spike; recorded time series above.
2026-08-04 15:02 - kv-sensitivity sweep added; 46% hit shows clear tail benefit.
2026-09-20 11:00 - short re-run for sanity after runtime kernel patch v0.9.3; numbers roughly match earlier with minor variance.

Practical recommendation (starter list)
- For latency-sensitive routes (chat frontend, interactive assistants): prefer dedicated pools with warm-size >=2 and aggressive prewarm for expected bursty customers. The cost delta is justified by tail reduction for UX-critical routes.
- For low-SLA bulk embedding or offline jobs: shared pool with opportunistic slots is still best for unit cost. Provide automatic route-level policy to switch during sustained spikes.
- Improve KV affinity tooling: expose affinity hints and prefetch primitives in the SDK so customers can push cache-hit rate higher easily.

Appendix: raw delim table (CSV) - sample data for quick ingestion
scenario,cache_hit,batch_ms,prewarm,preempt_level,p50,p95,p99,p999,gpu_min_per_1k,vcpu_min_per_1k,cost_per_1k
baseline,46,6,2,medium,48,92,160,430,2.6,4.8,3.2
shared_baseline,46,6,0,medium,51,112,260,960,1.9,5.2,2.7
dedicated_cold,12,6,0,low,60,150,420,1200,3.1,4.6,3.6
shared_burst,12,6,0,high,120,320,1100,3000,4.6,6.4,5.6

Last thoughts
These synthetic runs are intentionally small in scope but expose consistent storylines: tails are where UX breaks, and prewarm + cache are the most leverageable levers. We should convert this diary into a one-pager for the platform team with cut-down tables and a sparkline image for the console.

Contact
Ping me in #eng-observability or DM (Asha) for raw traces/links.

End of diary entry.
